title: Bongo (paired drums)
summary: The bongo is a pair of small drums joined by a wooden block, the small macho on the right and the larger hembra on the left. Held between the knees or set on a stand, and played with the fingers and palms, it carries the busy, bright fills of Cuban son and dance music.
howToPlay: Two heads are lit: the small macho on the right and the larger hembra on the left, each with a centre for an open tone and an outer ring for a slap.
A ring closes on the place to strike. Strike as it lands.
The rim of the small head gives a sharp click.
Start with the steady martillo, then add the slaps.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The patterns count four beats to the bar, played in eighth notes.
heritageNote: In Cuban son the bongo player keeps a steady eighth-note pattern called the martillo, the hammer, and breaks it with open tones and slaps. The two heads are tuned a fourth or fifth apart.
credits: Tradition: the bongo; patterns written for this game
